item.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption surveyed NSW public sector organisations and employees in 2007 about corruption risks and prevention practices.
item.support:
In 2007, the ICAC sent surveys examining corruption risks 
and corruption prevention strategies to NSW public sector 
organisations and staff.

item.text: ICAC reported responses from 317 organisations and 493 employees, covering organisational practices and staff perceptions across NSW.
item.support:
Responses were received from 317 
organisations and 493 staff.

item.text: ICAC reported that organisations most often identified procurement, recordkeeping and conflicts of interest as risks, while employees most often perceived favouritism and harassment as workplace problems.
item.support:
The risks most commonly identified 
by organisations include procurement, recordkeeping and 
conflicts of interest.

item.text: ICAC also reported gaps in staff awareness: 47% did not know they had to retain business emails and 36% had heard of the Protected Disclosures Act 1994.

item.quote:
Organisation responses indicated that high corruption 
risk functions are generally performed in the context of 
a policy framework.

Many organisations indicated that they have a variety 
of corruption prevention strategies in place but not 
all organisations use the same strategies.
